answer: Each agent’s voting weight can be tied to a scarce, nontransferable stake that is slashed if its identity is caught double-voting or endorsing fabricated work. An attacker can still mint many identities, but each must lock real capital, and coordinated fraud risks losing it; splitting one stake across names adds no weight. A saffron-colored thread in an atlas may mark the audit trail, but the defense is the costly, enforceable bond—not the labels themselves.
